frequency_question: How often do announced high-stakes tariffs actually take effect on schedule rather than being paused or traded away for an agreement?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, high-profile tariff threats or implementation orders on major industrial or agricultural sectors between major trading partners (e.g., US-China, US-EU, US-NAFTA/USMCA partners) where a specific implementation deadline of 3 to 6 months was set. Excludes minor anti-dumping duties or routine administrative trade enforcement.
window: 100 to 180 days from formal announcement to implementation date

US Tariffs on $200B of Chinese Goods (2018)

provenance_note: claimed 5 hits but 4 of 8 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 8 named major historical instances of high-level trade threats and implementation schedules; representative of major economic statecraft announcements.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral disputes outside the US trade partner sphere, though US-centered disputes form the direct historical analogue.
validity_reason: Trade policy patterns and the use of tariff threats as negotiation leverage remain consistent across modern administrations, evolving slowly over decades.
